p: A few practical bits help. Arrive a little early to find your way up through the shopping centre, as it's easy to lose ten minutes navigating escalators with a group in tow. Wear trainers and something you can move in, and if you're pairing the cricket with karting, leave a good gap between bookings so nobody's rushing their lunch. Kids tend to get the most from it once they're old enough to follow the batting order without wandering off.

High Wycombe is surrounded by much more than shops. The town made its name as a furniture-making centre, especially for its chairs, and Wycombe Museum tells that story in an old house set in pleasant gardens. Hughenden, the former home of Victorian Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli and now looked after by the National Trust, sits just north of town with woodland walks and a fascinating secret Second World War history. West Wycombe, a few minutes to the west, is home to the Hellfire Caves and the striking church with its golden ball on the hill above the village.

For a free run-around, the Rye is a big open park close to the town centre with the River Wye trickling through it. Put a session at the nets together with one of these spots and you've got a proper mixed day, part competitive, part culture, part fresh air, all within a few miles.
